I don't know that I'd say this is the FIRST. But this is probably one of my stronger memories of being wowed by a game.

It's 1997, I've got a Micron-built Pentium 166 MMX with 48mb of ram, 2gb of Hard Drive, and a Diamond Viper V550 video card, powered by an nVidia TNT chip, the caveman ancestor to the GeForce and by extension, modern GPUs. Despite the completely egregious load times whenever you hit a map seam, I remember sitting there with my buddy Jay, marveling at how pretty the game looked as you took the tram ride in to work.

Duke Nukem 3D was the first game where I was blown away, and it came with a level editor which got my 10 year old brain to start making my own virtual environments that I could create and change.

Goldeneye made me think that no game could ever be more realistic. I think when you play that game as a kid you still have a lot of imagination and that is how you view the game. I swear I remember shooting Russians in Goldeneye and seeing the expressions on their faces change as they died.

Half-Life came out when I was just the right age to want to dive into multiplayer. It was the first game where I found an actual online community via Planet Half-Life. I remember HL deathmatch blowing my mind, I was playing and talking with people from all over America and Europe. Duke3D had online but I only ever played it on a LAN with my brother. I remember when they released the SDK and then Team Fortress Classic which I played the hell out of and made a clan with the 2 or 3 kids from my high school that knew how to use a computer. Counter-Strike came out and that became the best game ever to play online. I would still say it is the ultimate best online game to challenge skill. I know the Call of Duty fags will always say the latest Call of Duty is the pinnacle of online FPS games, but no. Its Counter-Strike and it always has been Counter-Strike. If we play a Call of Duty match and you beat me, then it doesn't really mean anything. But if we play a Counter-Strike match and you beat me...I would respectfully bow to you like a Samurai because you bested me in a true test of skill.

Lastly I have to mention the original game Prey that came out in like 2006 or so. I remember that game had an actual PC demo that I downloaded. I remember the morning very well, as I was downloading the demo I thought I would eat some psilocybin mushrooms, that I had cause I was experimenting with growing them using online grow kits. I installed the demo and played the initial part where you are in the Indian bar for like a half an hour. I was getting a kick out of all the interactivity with the Jukebox and also I remember playing the arcade games-within-a-game that were in the bar. After like 30 minutes I activated the scripted sequence that began the alien abduction part. The mushrooms just started to kick in as I was teleported out of the bar onto this massive living space ship, every screaming and praying. It was one of the best beginnings of a game ever and it was heightened by 1000% since I was on mushrooms. It was amazing feeling like I am on this crazy alien ship that is abducting humans and killing people all over.

So I think if I had to choose eating mushrooms and playing the original Prey would be the best single video game experience I have ever had.
